document.title: OceanStor Pacific Series 8.1.0 (cluster-manager REST API, unofficial name)

capability_sources.note: Endpoint path and every field name used (id, name, management_ip, model, running_status, in_cluster, base_board, software_version, oam_agent_status, error_code, warranty_status) confirmed against a real, independently-authored, actively maintained Icinga/Nagios check-plugin script, not vendor prose alone -- Huawei's own TechDocs and administrator-guide pages returned empty content or HTTP 403 via automated fetch during connector construction. running_status was further confirmed as a lower-case string ('online'/'offline'), not a numeric code, by reading the shared huawei_pacific.py library's get_node_running_status_state() function directly. This connector only uses the confirmed identity fields and running_status; oam_agent_status, error_code, and warranty_status are real fields the plugin also reads but are not yet implemented here.

Endpoint path and field names (storagePoolId, storagePoolName, status, totalCapacity, usedCapacity) confirmed against the same real, maintained check-plugin script. The pool status code mapping (0=normal, 1=faulty, 2=write_protected, 3=stopped, 4=faulty_and_write_protected, 5=migrating, 7=degraded, 8=rebuilding) was confirmed by reading the shared huawei_pacific.py library's get_pool_status() function directly, the same rigor used for Dorado's HEALTHSTATUS mapping. This response's confirmed shape carries no result/error envelope (unlike cluster/servers), so this connector's response-envelope check is applied only when a result field is actually present.

authentication_source.note: Login request body fields (user_name, password, isEncrypt, scope) and the response token field (data.x_auth_token, used as the X-Auth-Token header on every subsequent request) confirmed by reading the shared library's get_creds() function directly. The logout endpoint (DELETE /api/v2/aa/sessions with the X-Auth-Token header, no body) was confirmed the same way, reading the library's _logout() function. This connector deliberately follows the Huawei Dorado candidate's design: a complete, bounded login -> read -> logout cycle inside the transport for every single read, never caching a live session, trading request volume for never holding a session open longer than one bounded operation. Simpler than Dorado in one respect: Pacific's confirmed auth needs only a header token, not a cookie.

self_test_source.note: No confirmed dedicated version/compatibility endpoint was found; the self-test reuses the cluster-node discovery read itself, the same pattern used for Brocade SANnav and Huawei Dorado.

unconfirmed_gaps: No default management port was confirmed for Pacific (unlike Dorado's documented 8088); the configuration schema requires it to be set explicitly rather than guessing.

The FusionStorage/DSware block-storage REST API family (used by the official OpenStack Cinder driver at api/v1/, with endpoints like /storagePool and /volume/create) is a genuinely different, separate API surface from the api/v2/ cluster-manager family this connector uses. Both were found to be real during construction, but only api/v2/ -- the one with confirmed health/status fields -- was used here; api/v1/ is documented for completeness but not implemented.
oam_agent_status, error_code, and warranty_status are real, confirmed node fields not yet surfaced by this connector's health mapping, which currently uses running_status only.
